summary: Interpreting broker artifact C1-lever-rule-sensitivity: under the stated closed, fixed-endpoint, two-phase assumptions, mass balance gives r=M_var/M_ref=[C_var,d+phi_l(C_var,l-C_var,d)]/[C_ref,d+phi_l(C_ref,l-C_ref,d)], with phi_l=(C_var,d-r*C_ref,d)/(r(C_ref,l-C_ref,d)-(C_var,l-C_var,d)) when defined and in [0,1]. Units check (uL)(ng/uL)=ng and normalized mass reconstruction residuals are at floating-point scale for reported valid points. For tie-line 0, K_ref=469.18 while K_var is undefined because both variant endpoints are zero; mixed x_var values .1-.9 are incompatible with those central endpoints. Tie-line 1 gives K_ref=238.54, K_var=9032.08 and K_var/K_ref=37.86; central valid points are x_var=.1 with phi_l=.99839 and .2 with .99194. Tie-line 2 gives K_ref=525.12, K_var=176.01 and K_var/K_ref=.335; central valid points are x_var=.3,.4,.5 with phi_l=.88327,.99562,.99921. Thus relative partition preference reverses across tie-lines and no universal monotone composition-to-cavity prediction follows. Marginal-error corner ranges are highly state-dependent and are sensitivity envelopes, not confidence intervals; some compositions become valid only at selected corners. The computation does not check an explicit equal-partition synthetic limit, and phase volume remains unmapped to f. H1 remains a conditional hypothesis, not an explanation confirmed for B; H2 remains viable.

candidates.target: Explain emergence and persistence of internal RNA-poor cavities, using f(t), the arithmetic mean of per-droplet segmented internal dark-area fractions; 36/48 h measurements remain reserved.
known_relations: Observed E01: A f falls from 0.01487 at 0 h to about 0.0044 at 8-24 h; B rises from 0.01381 to 0.08918 by 24 h. Seven fields per condition pool two preparations, so field/object counts are not independent preparation replicates.
Observed E02: endpoint f medians M=2.785e-5, M+L=0.04446, M+S=0.09412; length fractions lack precise mixture ratios, RNA yield, time course and carryover matching.

Observed E04/C04: three endpoint tie-lines give reference and variant RNA concentrations in dilute/dense phases, with broad supplied marginal error bounds; no phase volumes, time-resolved B RNA composition, cavity-local composition or link to f.
Observed E03: aggregate motion summaries differ, but no same-droplet cavity-state trajectory is supplied.

Computed C1 conditionally: tie-line 1 has K_var/K_ref=37.86; tie-line 2 has 0.335; tie-line 0 variant partition ratio is undefined. Under fixed endpoints, lever-rule-compatible global mass-fraction ranges differ by tie-line; this is not a B measurement.

Unknown: whether DNA variants are transcribed and at what RNA mass fractions; whether E04's variant is the relevant species; which phase, if any, is the cavity; and how phase volume/geometry maps to f.
hypotheses: H1 (new, explicit, unverified and conditional): if the measured reference and variant RNAs form two coexisting phases with fixed tie-line endpoints and one phase occupies the internal RNA-poor compartment, global RNA mass composition constrains the phase volume fraction by mass balance. The direction and compatible composition interval depend on the tie-line because relative partition preference reverses between tie-lines 1 and 2. A corresponding change in measured cavity f requires additional geometry and identity assumptions and is not derived here.

H2 (alternative): age-dependent or amplification carryover changes transcription or material state and causes cavitation without variant-specific partition enrichment; at matched age and carryover, changing RNA composition alone need not produce systematic cavity enrichment.

gaps.description: Establish whether differential partitioning can be connected to an internal RNA-poor compartment and measured f, and whether the conditional lever-rule signature is physically applicable. C1 computes phase-volume consequences but cannot identify cavity identity, causal effects in B, or an image-area mapping; an explicit equal-partition limit check is still needed.

variables_units.f: dimensionless arithmetic mean over droplets of segmented internal dark area / filled area
variables_units.C_ref,d,C_var,d,C_ref,l,C_var,l: ng/uL measured E04 endpoint concentrations in dense (d) and dilute (l) phases
variables_units.K_i: dimensionless dense/dilute concentration ratio C_i,d/C_i,l, undefined when C_i,l=0
variables_units.x_var: dimensionless variant fraction by RNA mass in the total mixture; hypothetical input, not known from DNA reads
variables_units.r: dimensionless global variant/reference RNA mass ratio x_var/(1-x_var)
variables_units.phi_l: dimensionless dilute-phase volume fraction; hypothetical and not the image-area statistic
variables_units.M_ref,M_var: ng total species masses, with M_i=V_d*C_i,d+V_l*C_i,l

equations: For species i, M_i=V_d*C_i,d+V_l*C_i,l (ng = uL * ng/uL).

Let phi_l=V_l/(V_d+V_l), delta_i=C_i,l-C_i,d, and r=M_var/M_ref. Then r=[C_var,d+phi_l*delta_var]/[C_ref,d+phi_l*delta_ref], hence phi_l=(C_var,d-r*C_ref,d)/(r*delta_ref-delta_var), when the denominator is nonzero and 0<=phi_l<=1. Equivalently x_var=M_var/(M_ref+M_var), so r=x_var/(1-x_var).
The lever rule requires fixed coexisting endpoint concentrations and no additional species or phase; endpoint data alone do not determine phi_l because r is unknown.
Measured image observable remains f=mean_j(A_internal,j/A_filled,j); no equality between f and phi_l is assumed.
parameters_ranges: C1 evaluated x_var=0,.1,...,1 for each E04 tie-line using central endpoints; only values with 0<=phi_l<=1 are compatible with that fixed tie-line.

A discriminating future observation would quantify RNA species mass fractions in internal and outer/dilute regions and f in matched droplets/preparations over time, while holding age, total RNA and carryover fixed.

Population composition, droplet selection, segmentation or changing filled-area denominators can alter aggregate f without within-droplet phase growth.
predictions: Conditional H1: if an E04-like tie-line applies, independently measured x_var must lie in its compatible range and determines phi_l; the tie-line-specific species concentrations predict which RNA is enriched in each phase. Tie-line 1 and tie-line 2 imply opposite relative variant/reference dense-phase preferences.

A matched composition series measuring internal-phase species enrichment and f distinguishes these accounts; absence of enrichment weakens H1, while f alone does not identify it.
No 36/48 h time extrapolation is committed.

Tie-line 0 variant is absent in both phases, so it cannot define variant partition preference or mixed-composition behavior.
E02 endpoint differences are compatible with composition effects but do not isolate composition from preparation, RNA yield or carryover.
E04 marginal uncertainty is broad and does not establish morphology, cavity identity, B composition or causality.
